column1: unstinting§Her unstinting support for junior colleagues cost her four promotions and built nine careers.§她对年轻同事**毫不吝惜的**支持让她失去四次升职，成就了九个人的事业。§un（不）+ stint（吝惜）
unsubstantiated§The unsubstantiated claim was repeated in nine outlets and corrected, four months later, in one.§这项**未经证实的**说法被九家媒体转载，四个月后只有一家更正。§
unsuitable§The site was unsuitable for four documented reasons, and the planning permission was granted anyway.§这块地因四条有据可查的理由而**不适合**，规划许可还是批了。§
unsure§She was unsure about the date and certain about everything else, which the jury found persuasive.§她对日期**没有把握**，对其余一切都确定，陪审团觉得这很有说服力。§
unswerving§His unswerving attention to one question for nine years produced the four papers everyone now cites.§他九年**毫不动摇地**盯住一个问题，产出了如今人人引用的四篇论文。§un（不）+ swerve（偏离）
unvaried§The unvaried diet of the crew explains the illness that four doctors had failed to diagnose.§船员**一成不变的**饮食解释了四位医生未能诊断出的那种病。§
unverified§The unverified figure appeared in nine reports and originated, it turned out, in a typing error.§这个**未经核实的**数字出现在九份报告里，而它原来源于一处打字错误。§
unwieldy§The unwieldy document runs to nine hundred pages and is consulted, in practice, four pages at a time.§这份**笨重难用的**文件长达九百页，实际使用时一次只查四页。§un（不）+ wieldy（好使的）
unwitting§He was an unwitting participant for four years and reported the scheme within nine days of understanding it.§他**不知情地**参与了四年，弄明白后九天内就举报了这个计划。§un（不）+ wit（知道，同 witness 证人）
unyielding§Her unyielding position on one clause cost nine months and, in the end, won the point.§她在一条条款上**毫不让步的**立场耗掉九个月，最终赢得了这一点。§un（不）+ yield（屈服）
uplift§Four hundred pounds of paint uplifted a stairwell that nine hundred people use every day.§四百英镑的油漆**提振**了一处每天九百人使用的楼梯间。§up（向上）+ lift（举）
uprise§A local uprising in four villages had spread to nine towns before the government admitted anything was happening.§四个村庄的一场**起义**已蔓延到九个镇，政府才承认有事发生。§up（向上）+ rise（升起）
urgency§The urgency was manufactured: the deadline had been moved forward four months for no stated reason.§这种**紧迫**是制造出来的——期限被无故提前了四个月。§urg（推动，同 urge 催促）
usurp§Four officials usurped a power that the statute gives, quite plainly, to an elected committee.§四名官员**篡夺**了法条明白无误地赋予一个民选委员会的权力。§us（使用）+ rap（抓取，同 rapid 迅速的）→ 抓来自用
usurper§The usurper governed competently for nine years and is remembered only for how he arrived.§这位**篡位者**称职地治理了九年，而人们只记得他是怎么上台的。§
utilitarian§The utilitarian argument favours the cheaper option, and four ethicists have written to say why it should not.§**功利主义的**论证支持较便宜的选项，四位伦理学家撰文说明为何不该如此。§util（有用，同 utility 效用）
vacillate§He vacillated for nine months, and by the time he chose, both options had been withdrawn.§他**摇摆不定**了九个月，等他做选择时两个选项都已撤回。§vacill（摇晃）
vacillation§The vacillation cost more than either decision would have, which is the report's central point.§这种**犹豫不决**的代价超过任何一个决定，这是报告的核心观点。§
vacuous§The statement is vacuous: nine sentences, four of them adjectives, and no commitment at all.§这份声明**空洞无物**——九个句子，四句是形容词堆砌，毫无承诺。§vac（空，同 vacant 空的）
vagary§The vagaries of the funding cycle decide more careers here than the quality of anyone's work.§经费周期的**反复无常**在这里决定的职业生涯，比任何人工作的质量决定的还多。§vag（游荡，同 vague 模糊的）
vagueness§The vagueness is deliberate: four agencies can each read the clause as protecting their own position.§这种**含糊**是刻意的——四家机构各自都能把这条读成保护自己的立场。§
validate§Four independent tests validated the method, and the fifth found the effect only in warm weather.§四项独立测试**验证**了这个方法，第五项发现该效应只在温暖天气出现。§valid（有效）
validity§The validity of the survey depends on a response rate of forty percent, and this one reached nine.§这项调查的**有效性**取决于百分之四十的回复率，而这次只到九。§
valor§His valor was recorded in four citations, and he refused to discuss it for the next ninety years.§他的**英勇**记载在四份嘉奖令里，而他此后九十年拒绝谈论此事。§val（力量，同 valid 有效的）
vanquish§A team of nine amateurs vanquished four professional sides in a single season and then disbanded.§一支九人的业余队伍在一个赛季**击败**了四支职业队，随后解散了。§vinc（征服，同 victory 胜利）
vapid§The vapid opening chapter deters most readers before the book becomes genuinely good on page ninety.§**乏味的**开头一章劝退了多数读者，而这本书在第九十页才真正好起来。§vap（走气）
variegate§Frost variegates the leaves in a way no gardener has managed to reproduce on purpose.§霜把叶片**染成斑驳**，而没有园丁能刻意复制这种效果。§vari（变化，同 various 各种的）
vector§The mosquito is the vector, and eliminating it in four districts cut cases by about ninety percent.§蚊子是**传播媒介**，在四个区消灭它使病例减少了约九成。§vect（携带，同 convey 传送）
veer§The road veers north for four miles for no reason anyone can now explain.§这条路向北**偏转**四英里，如今没人能解释原因。§
venality§The venality of the office was an open secret for nine years and cost four hundred thousand pounds.§这个衙门的**贪腐**九年来是公开的秘密，代价是四十万英镑。§ven（出售）→ 官职可卖
venerability§The venerability of the institution is four hundred years old and its filing system is nearly as old.§这家机构的**德高望重**有四百年之久，而它的归档系统也差不多同样古老。§
venerate§Students venerated a teacher who had, according to nine of them, never once raised his voice.§学生们**敬重**这位老师，据其中九人说，他从未提高过嗓门。§vener（敬爱）
veneration§The veneration surrounding the founder made it impossible, for forty years, to audit his accounts.§围绕创始人的**崇敬**让人四十年无法审计他的账目。§
vengeful§The vengeful memo was written at four in the morning and sent, unfortunately, at four in the morning.§这份**报复性的**备忘录写于凌晨四点，不幸也在凌晨四点发出。§veng（复仇，同 revenge 复仇）
verbalization§Verbalization of the rule took nine years, and everyone had followed it perfectly well before that.§把这条规则**诉诸文字**花了九年，而在此之前人人都遵守得很好。§verb（词语，同 verbal 口头的）
verbose§The verbose report says in nine hundred words what the covering email said in four lines.§这份**冗长的**报告用九百字说的，附信里四行就说完了。§verb（词语，同 verbal 口头的）
verdant§The verdant slopes in the photograph are, for nine months of the year, bare rock.§照片里**苍翠的**山坡，一年中有九个月是光秃的岩石。§verd（绿）
verisimilitude§The verisimilitude of the forgery was its weakness: it matched the period four decades too precisely.§这件伪作的**逼真**正是它的弱点——它与那个时代吻合得精确了四十年不止。§veri（真实，同 verify 核实）+ simil（相似）
versatility§Her sheer versatility kept the whole department running through nine months in which four posts stood vacant.§她过人的**多面手**能力让整个系在四个岗位空缺的九个月里维持了运转。§vers（转，同 reverse 倒转）→ 转得开
vestige§Not a vestige of the original interior survives, and the four photographs are all we have.§原始室内没有留下一点**痕迹**，我们所有的只是四张照片。§vestig（足迹，同 investigate 调查）
vestigial§The vestigial wing is useless for flight and, in four species, still used for display.§这只**退化的**翅膀不能飞行，而在四个物种中仍用于展示。§
vet§Four lawyers vetted the contract, and the clause that ended the partnership survived all four readings.§四位律师**审查**过这份合同，而终结合伙关系的那条挺过了全部四轮审读。§
vex§The question vexed the field for ninety years and was settled, in the end, by a photograph.§这个问题**困扰**了这个领域九十年，最终被一张照片解决。§vex（摇撼）
viable§The plan is viable only if four separate approvals arrive in the same nine-week window.§这个方案只有在四项独立批准都落在同一个九周窗口内时才**可行**。§vi（生命）→ 活得下来
vibrant§The vibrant street of the 1970s is now four takeaways and a betting shop.§1970 年代那条**生机勃勃的**街道，如今是四家外卖店和一间投注站。§vibr（震动，同 vibrate 振动）
vicarious§The pleasure was vicarious and no less real: she had trained nine of the eleven finalists.§这份快乐是**替代性的**，却同样真实——十一位决赛选手中有九位是她训练的。§vicari（代替，同 vice- 副）
vicious§The vicious circle here is simple enough: fewer buses means fewer riders, which in turn means fewer buses.§这里的**恶性**循环很简单——车少则乘客少，乘客少又意味着车更少。§vic（缺陷，同 vice 恶习）
vigilant§Four vigilant residents noticed the smoke, and the fire brigade arrived within nine minutes.§四位**警觉的**居民注意到了烟，消防队九分钟内赶到。§vigil（警醒，同 vigil 守夜）
vignette§The vignette on page four does more work than the nine pages of analysis that follow it.§第四页的这则**小品文**起的作用超过其后九页的分析。§
vile§The vile conditions were reported in 1908, in 1974, and again nine years ago.§这些**恶劣至极的**条件在 1908 年、1974 年和九年前都被报告过。§vil（低贱）
vilify§Newspapers vilified her for four years and, after the acquittal, printed nine words of apology.§报纸**诋毁**了她四年，在无罪判决后印了九个字的道歉。§vil（低贱）+ fy（使）
villainous§The villainous landlord of the pamphlet turns out, in the archives, to have been four separate men.§小册子里那个**恶棍般的**房东，在档案中原来是四个不同的人。§
vindicate§Nine years of records vindicated a man whose case had rested on nobody believing him.§九年的记录**证明**了一个人的清白，而他的案子此前只靠没人相信他。§vin ← vim（力量）+ dic（说，同 dictate 口述）→ 用言辞讨回公道
vindication§The vindication came four years after his death, and the family had stopped expecting it.§这份**平反**在他去世四年后到来，家人早已不再期待。§
vindictive§The vindictive clause served no purpose except to cost the other side about four hundred pounds.§这条**报复性的**条款除了让对方损失约四百英镑，别无用处。§
violently§The market moved violently for nine days and settled, in the end, four points from where it started.§市场**剧烈**波动九天，最终收在距起点四个点的位置。§viol（暴力，同 violate 违反）
virtuosity§The virtuosity is real and beside the point: the piece needs four seconds of silence it never gets.§这份**精湛技艺**是真的，也无关紧要——这首曲子需要四秒它从未得到的静默。§virtu（才艺）
viscous§The fluid is viscous below four degrees, which is why the pump failed on nine winter mornings.§这种液体在四度以下**黏稠**，这就是泵在九个冬日清晨故障的原因。§visc（黏）
visionary§The visionary plan of 1908 was rejected, and four of its nine proposals were built after 1970.§1908 年那个**有远见的**方案被否决，其九项提议中的四项在 1970 年后建成。§vis（看，同 vision 视觉）
vitiate§One unchecked assumption in the second chapter vitiates nine years of otherwise scrupulously careful work.§第二章里一个未经核实的假设**毁掉**了九年在其他方面一丝不苟的工作。§viti（缺陷，同 vice 恶习）
vitriolic§The vitriolic review ended a career, and the book it attacked is now on four university syllabuses.§这篇**尖酸刻薄的**评论终结了一段事业，而它攻击的书如今在四所大学的教学大纲上。§vitriol（硫酸）→ 像强酸一样腐蚀
vivacious§The vivacious host kept nine strangers talking for four hours and remembered every name.§这位**活泼热络的**主人让九位陌生人聊了四小时，还记住了每个名字。§viv（生命，同 survive 幸存）
vocal§The four most vocal opponents had each, at some point, proposed something very similar.§四位**嗓门最大的**反对者，都曾在某个时候提出过非常相似的东西。§voc（声音，同 voice 声音）
vocalize§She vocalizes the objection that nine other people in the room have decided not to raise.§她**说出**了屋里另外九个人决定不提的那条反对意见。§
voluble§The voluble witness said a great deal in four hours and confirmed almost nothing.§这位**滔滔不绝的**证人四小时里说了很多，几乎什么也没证实。§volv（转，同 revolve 旋转）→ 话滚滚而出
voluminous§The voluminous correspondence runs to nine boxes, and four of them have never been opened.§这批**卷帙浩繁的**信件装了九箱，其中四箱从未打开过。§volum（卷轴，同 volume 卷）
voracious§A voracious reader at nine, she had finished four of the four hundred books by that winter.§九岁就是**如饥似渴的**读者，到那年冬天她已读完四百本中的四百本。§vor（吞食，同 carnivorous 食肉的）
